LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.empiricalPMF: For blocklength n > 0, the empirical law of a type t assigns each symbol a its count t(a) divided by n.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.empiricalPMF_appl: For n > 0, the mass of a under the empirical law of t is exactly t(a)/n.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mem_support_empir: For n > 0, a symbol a belongs to the support of the empirical law of t if and only if its count t(a) is positive.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.wordTypeEquivPMF: For length n > 0 on a finite alphabet, the type with counts c(a) maps to its empirical law p(a) = c(a)/n. This is a bijection onto the laws that admit n as a common denominator, meaning that n p(a) is a nonnegative integer for every letter a. The counts sum to n.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.wordTypeEquivPMF_: For n > 0, the law associated to type t by the type–law bijection is its empirical distribution.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mem_typeClass_iff: For n > 0, a word x belongs to the type class of t if and only if the empirical distribution of x equals that of t.
